evidence.summary: Forge construction and projection timings show duplicate recovery/query work was eliminated.
A generation publication extends the verified projection without rereading old object payloads.
Stranded verifier recovery loads one bounded action/result view and reuses the generation-bound projection.
The final 25-iteration benchmark reached its declared 300 s limit in native SSA/Store runtime work.

reproduction.instructions: Use the controlled Store-backed Forge workspace with native Store semantics; measure Store session construction, one open-time verification, Forge projection construction, warm records(), stranded-action recovery, continuous start, and the 300 s micro-verifier benchmark. Confirm that no host-side hash fallback is used.

summary: Duplicate Store recovery, current-generation verification, Forge projection, and stranded-action scans were removed from the Store-backed startup path. Forge construction fell from 186.1-187.2 s to 44.97-45.88 s, and warm projection queries fell from about 24 s to about 0.00003 s. Native Store SHA/runtime still dominates cold publication and the 300 s micro-verifier benchmark remains timed out.

workaround.description: Keep one resident supervisor and reuse generation-bound Store projections; native Store/runtime work still needs a measured follow-up optimization.
